model: Regulated utility FCFE (attributable net income less equity-funded rate-base growth) at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,164.26M shares outstanding at 30 Sep 2026 (10-Q cover) plus ~3M treasury-method dilution from stock-based awards (Q3-2026 diluted-EPS table). Held FLAT: future ATM/forward-sale and equity-unit issuance is charged in the flows as a negative (FCFE = net income less the full increase in common equity, however funded), so growing the count as well would double-count it. No forward-sale shares remained unsettled at 30 Sep 2026.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow statement 'Stock based compensation expense': FY2025 136 (SO_Annual_FY2025.txt:25804), 9M-2026 139 vs 9M-2025 124 (SO_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt cash flow) -> TTM 151. No separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed. Net income is already after this expense; the sbc path exists only so the street memo can add it back.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field is a COST OF EQUITY, because the flows are post-interest equity flows. 7.5% = ~4.3% 10-year US Treasury + ~0.6 regulated-utility beta x ~5% US equity risk premium, rounded up; USD flows, USD rate. The same 7.5% is used in all three scenarios -- regulatory and execution risk is charged in the scenario ROE/growth paths and the bear weight, not a second time in the rate.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: net_debt is held at ZERO in the engine. The flow is net income attributable to common (after $3.2bn/yr of interest) less the equity-funded share of rate-base growth, so the $74.0bn of debt (securities due within one year 3,613 + notes payable 890 + long-term debt 69,498) is already paid for inside the flow. Subtracting it again would deduct the debt twice. total_debt and cash are recorded for reference only.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not modelled separately: operating lease obligations (~$1.5bn) are immaterial against $164bn of assets and their cost is inside net income.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Net income is 'Consolidated Net Income Attributable to Southern Company' (after the noncontrolling-interest line) and the equity base is common stockholders' equity of $42,056m = total stockholders' equity $44,806m less $2,750m noncontrolling interests (mostly Southern Power tax-equity and joint-ownership partners). Nothing is deducted for NCI in the bridge. Note the NCI line flipped sign after Southern Power bought out the SP Wind tax-equity partner on 31 Dec 2025: 9M-2025 NCI absorbed a $95m LOSS (HLBV allocations, which flattered attributable income), 9M-2026 NCI took $24m of INCOME. The forward ROE path is anchored on 2026-28 guidance, which is post-buyout.
inputs.notes: MODEL: equity-flow (FCFE) valuation at the cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net debt at zero -- NOT the unlevered owner-FCF DCF. Reason: Southern is a rate-regulated utility in a capex supercycle (TTM operating cash flow $10.5bn vs property additions $14.2bn; reported FCF negative in 16 of the last 19 years). Unlevered FCF less $72bn net debt gives a meaningless negative number, because the capex is not a cost -- it is rate base that earns an allowed return and is financed ~55-60% with debt by regulatory design. The flow that accrues to shareholders is: attributable net income minus the increase in common equity needed to hold the capital structure as rate base grows = dividends minus net new share issuance. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue grows at the common-equity (rate-base) growth rate with revenue/common-equity held at the TTM 0.742x; 'ebitda_margin' = attributable net-income margin + the SBC add-back = ROE / (0.742 x (1+g)) + 0.48; 'capex' = equity reinvestment = g / (0.742 x (1+g)); D&A and tax are zero because net income is already after both. So year-t flow = (ROE on opening common equity - g) x opening common equity. Year 1 is approximately calendar 2027. last_fcf is the TTM equity flow on this definition (attributable NI 4,993 less the 7,054 increase in common equity, which included $3.8bn of forward-sale settlements pulled into 2026); it is negative because 2026 front-loaded most of the ~$5bn equity plan, and it is not the base the projection compounds from. reported_fcf is TTM OCF 10,477 less property additions 14,235. GUIDANCE ANCHOR (Q3-2026 call via Analysis JSON, not in the 10-Q): FY2026 adjusted EPS ~4.70; FY2027 4.85-4.95 and FY2028 5.25-5.45, both flagged for a raise; 8-9% EPS CAGR 2026-28, 7-8% thereafter to 2030; $81bn 2026-30 capex; dividend 3.04/share. Base year-1 net income of ~$5.8bn (~$4.95/share on ~1,172m average shares) and year-2 ~$6.36bn (~$5.36) sit inside those ranges. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print. Buybacks: none (the company is a net issuer). Because SBC is ~0.5% of revenue, house and street values are close and the band is narrow.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management rate-base/capex plan ($81bn 2026-30) and 8-9% EPS guidance, not a trailing CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (3.8%, total equity incl. NCI, FY2020-FY2025) is more than 30% below the EPS 5yr CAGR (6.0%) and far below the forward plan. The trailing equity CAGR spans the Vogtle write-off years and predates the 2026 equity raise ($3.8bn settled in nine months; common equity +17% since Dec 2025), so it understates the forward rate-base growth; it was not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: reported FCF (OCF less property additions) is negative in both endpoint years (FY2022 -1,621, FY2025 -2,935) and structurally negative for a utility funding rate-base growth externally. SBC (~$135m/yr, flat for three years) is immaterial to the trend. Revenue CAGRs are distorted by fuel-cost pass-through (FY2022 gas-price spike).

base.roe_on_opening_common_equity_note: 13.8, 14.0, 14.0, 13.8, 13.5, 13.2, 13.0, 12.8, 12.5, 12.5 percent. Adjusted ROE on average common equity ran ~13.7-13.9% in 2024-2026E (opco allowed/earned ROEs of ~10.5-12% plus holding-company leverage); the path fades 1.3pp as parent leverage is rebuilt with equity and post-2028 rate cases share large-load margins with customers.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 3% growth and 7.5% cost of equity binds (22.9x the net equity flow, below the 24x cap) = ~17x terminal earnings and ~2.1x book, against ~20x and 2.6x today.

scenario_narratives.base: The $81bn 2026-30 plan is built broadly as filed: common equity (rate base at a held capital structure) grows ~8% a year through 2029, funded by ~5% retained earnings plus $1-1.5bn a year of ATM/equity-unit issuance, then decelerates toward 3% by year 10 as the generation build for the ~21GW of contracted large load completes. ROE on opening common equity holds ~14% through the Georgia base-rate freeze (to 2028), delivering EPS at the upper half of the 2027-28 guidance ranges, then fades to 12.5% as the 2028 Georgia rate case and the large-load settlement hand part of the data-center margin back to residential customers and parent leverage is diluted with equity. The incoming Georgia governor slows but does not stop new large-load siting.
scenario_narratives.bull: More of the 75GW+ pipeline converts to contracts, the capital plan steps up again (as it has three times since February 2025: $63bn -> $76bn -> $81bn), and equity grows 9-9.5% a year through 2030. Large-load contracts with minimum bills earn at or above the allowed return, the Georgia PSC stays constructive in the 2028 case, the new build avoids Vogtle-style overruns, and ROE on opening equity holds 14-14.5% before fading to 13%. Faster growth lowers the near-term net payout (more issuance) but compounds a larger equity base earning well above its cost.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Georgia political turn becomes policy: a data-center moratorium or tighter cost-allocation rules under the new governor and a less friendly PSC cut large-load additions, hyperscaler AI capex retrenches and some contracted load is deferred, so equity growth falls to 6.5% and then 3-4%. The 2028 Georgia rate case resets the allowed return and disallows part of any cost overrun, a Moody's downgrade raises parent financing costs, and ROE on opening common equity slides from 13.3% to 10.5% -- roughly a bare allowed ROE with no holding-company uplift. The dividend is still covered; this is a de-rating case (terminal ~14x earnings, ~1.4x book), not a solvency case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the incremental earnings depend on a single regulator (Georgia PSC) and a single demand driver (data centers), and the adverse political event has already happened -- a governor-elect who campaigned on a data-center moratorium and affordability -- alongside a negative Moody's outlook. Base at 50%: guidance has been raised repeatedly, base rates are frozen through 2028 and ~21GW is under contract. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs the pipeline to convert, the PSC to stay constructive through the 2028 case, and a very large generation build to land on budget, all at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Southern is valued as what it is: a levered claim on a regulated asset base that earns ~12.5-14% on common equity against a ~7.5% cost of equity, and can reinvest at that spread for as long as regulators let rate base grow. Value is the present value of what shareholders actually net out -- dividends less the new equity they are asked to fund. On that basis the shares are worth roughly their market price in the base case; the price already pays for the 8-9% growth guidance, and the asymmetry is to the downside because the bear case (regulatory reset of ROE) removes the spread on the whole equity base, while the bull case only adds growth at the margin. A 15% hurdle is not available from this asset at anything near the current price; the entry price is shown for consistency with the rest of the folder, and the required-return table is the more useful read.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: the model discounts at 7.5%; value falls steeply with the rate because ~75% of it is terminal (see the sensitivity grid). A 100bp rise in long rates is worth more than the bull-base gap.
Terminal ROE spread: the base case assumes Southern still earns 12.5% on common equity in year 10 (~2.1x book). The bear case shows what a reset to 10.5% costs.
Georgia regulatory and political risk: governor-elect's data-center moratorium platform, the July 2028 base-rate case, and cost allocation of the generation build.

Equity issuance price: the flat share count assumes new shares are issued at about fair value; issuance below intrinsic value (a stressed raise after a downgrade) would transfer value away from existing holders.
Adjusted vs GAAP earnings: guidance is on adjusted EPS (FY2026 ~4.70 vs TTM GAAP 4.36); recurring 'non-recurring' charges would lower the realised ROE.
Execution: Vogtle 3&4 cost $36.8bn against a ~$14bn plan; a disallowed overrun on the new build comes straight out of equity.
